scope: Supervised macOS qualification stages for ca-3d-m6: the tiny parity probes from the structural probe bundle and the cavern chambers; one bounded stage per receipt, not release acceptance
host: Apple M3 Ultra, macOS 26.6.2, owned headless Chrome under scripts.verification_guard (kind macos-qualification, 300 s), Metal WebGPU

records.probeScope: 8^3 and 16^3 ca-3d-m6 fixtures, GPU equal to the CPU oracle after every tick; not larger worlds, frames or gameplay
8^3 and 16^3 ca-3d-m6 fixtures, GPU equal to the CPU oracle after every tick; not larger worlds, frames or gameplay

retention: Gameplay and tiny-probe reports and every supervisor receipt are retained in full. The nine replay reports carry 1,025 reference digests and about 2,000 per-tick GPU checks each, so only their SHA-256, windows, runs and tick-end digest are kept here; the raw files remain in dist/verification on the workstation and any stage is reproducible with npm run verify:macos -- --stage <name>. sourceHashesSha256 is the SHA-256 of each report's sourceHashes map serialized with sorted keys and no whitespace; sourceSets lists the two sets and the hashed paths that differ between them.

sourceSets.note: The first twelve chamber stages, run on one source set whose tracked files are the tree that introduced the stages. The six 64^3 receipts and their 32^3 prerequisites are retained from this set; the 64^3 stages were not rerun afterwards because the follow-up launched nothing above 32^3.

The tiny parity probes and the six 32^3 chamber stages rerun on the final sources of the branch: the shared Python interpreter resolver, the m6-tiny stages and the probe bundle rebuilt from them. Each 32^3 replay ends in the same tick-1,024 digest as its first-set run.
